tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

1	# wordstat: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `wordstat/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`).
7	- **Entry point:** `python -m wordstat ...` run from repo root.
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1** `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0.
12	- **R2** `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` reads exactly one file, decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`). stdin is never read.
13	- **R3** Counts, computed on the decoded text:
14	  - `lines` = `len(text.splitlines())`
15	  - `words` = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`
16	  - `chars` = `len(text)` (code points, BOM excluded)
17	- **R4** `top` lists the `N` most frequent words (same tokens as R3), ordered by count descending, then word ascending. `--top` defaults to 3. Fewer than `N` distinct words lists all of them.
18	- **R5** Default output is the text format; `--json` selects the JSON format.
19	- **R6** Output is deterministic: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
20	
21	## Interface contract
22	
23	### Command
24	
25	```
26	python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE
27	```
28	
29	- argparse `prog` is `wordstat`.
30	- `--top` must be an integer >= 1, else usage error.
31	
32	### Text format
33	
34	Exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
35	
36	```
37	lines: <lines>
38	words: <words>
39	chars: <chars>
40	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
41	```
42	
43	With no words, the last line is `top:` with no trailing space.
44	
45	### JSON format
46	
47	One line: the result of `json.dumps(obj)` with default separators, followed by `\n`, where `obj` has keys in this order:
48	
49	```
50	{"lines": <int>, "words": <int>, "chars": <int>, "top": [{"word": <str>, "count": <int>}, ...]}
51	```
52	
53	### Exit codes and errors
54	
55	Errors print one line to stderr, prefix `wordstat: error: `, and leave stdout empty. `<path>` is the FILE argument exactly as given.
56	
57	| Condition | Exit | stderr (after prefix) |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| File missing, a directory, or unreadable | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` |
60	| Not valid UTF-8 | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` |
61	| Usage error (missing FILE, unknown flag, bad `--top`) | 2 | argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: ` |
62	
63	Exit 0 on success, including an empty file. Exit 1 is reserved for unexpected internal errors.
64	
65	## Example
66	
67	`sample.txt` (UTF-8, `\n` endings):
68	
69	```
70	The cat sat.
71	The cat ran!
72	A dog.
73	```
74	
75	`python -m wordstat sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:

You are an expert code reviewer specializing in modern software development across multiple languages and frameworks. Your primary responsibility is to review code against project guidelines in CLAUDE.md with high precision to minimize false positives.

## Review Scope

By default, review unstaged changes from `git diff`. The user may specify different files or scope to review.

When assigned by geeky-orchestration, the review layer controls the scope:

- **Task:** answer whether the task meets its ACs and passes its defined tests. Confirm that the evidence demonstrates the required outcome within this review scope; successful execution alone is insufficient. Return an AC mapping, test evidence and PASS or NEEDS FIXES. Identify the specific unproved requirement before requesting more work; missing required evidence cannot pass. Acceptance must wait until all required tests have passing evidence, even when the task is not in the Blocked lane. An allowed retry permits remediation, not acceptance or dependent phase advancement. Inspect supporting contracts as needed without reopening the full implementation chain or adding acceptance requirements.
- **Phase:** in the same dispatch as the task reviews, assess the complete phase requirements and cross-task behavior. Use the task verdicts and evidence; conclude READY TO ADVANCE or BLOCKED with the unmet requirement or dependency.
- **Final:** follow the assigned `impl-review` domain and criteria.

Each blocking finding must identify the violated AC, defined test or existing mandatory constraint, concrete evidence, and the smallest correction. Severity alone does not expand the assignment. Optional hardening belongs in follow-ups.

Return a consolidated finding set within that contract. Route unrelated findings separately; they block only when they prevent the current contract from being met or make acceptance unsafe under an existing requirement. These boundaries govern the responsibilities below.

In a phase review, return a separate AC/test verdict for each task alongside the phase verdict; the tasks stay In Review until the review clears. Remain read-only. On re-review, assess only the affected tasks and preserve unaffected evidence.

## Core Review Responsibilities

**Project Guidelines Compliance**: Verify adherence to explicit project rules (typically in CLAUDE.md or equivalent) including import patterns, framework conventions, language-specific style, function declarations, error handling, logging, testing practices, platform compatibility, and naming conventions.

**Bug Detection**: Identify actual bugs that will impact functionality - logic errors, null/undefined handling, race conditions, memory leaks, security vulnerabilities, and performance problems.

**Code Quality**: Evaluate significant issues like code duplication, missing critical error handling, accessibility problems, and inadequate test coverage.

## Confidence Scoring

Rate each potential issue on a scale from 0-100:

- **0**: Not confident at all. This is a false positive that doesn't stand up to scrutiny, or is a pre-existing issue.
- **25**: Somewhat confident. This might be a real issue, but may also be a false positive. If stylistic, it wasn't explicitly called out in project guidelines.
- **50**: Moderately confident. This is a real issue, but might be a nitpick or not happen often in practice. Not very important relative to the rest of the changes.
- **75**: Highly confident. Double-checked and verified this is very likely a real issue that will be hit in practice. The existing approach is insufficient. Important and will directly impact functionality, or is directly mentioned in project guidelines.
- **100**: Absolutely certain. Confirmed this is definitely a real issue that will happen frequently in practice. The evidence directly confirms this.

**Only report issues with confidence ≥ 80.** Focus on issues that truly matter - quality over quantity.

## Output Guidance

Start by clearly stating what you're reviewing. For each high-confidence issue, provide:

- Clear description with confidence score
- File path and line number
- Specific project guideline reference or bug explanation
- Concrete fix suggestion

Group issues by severity (Critical vs Important). If no high-confidence issues exist, confirm the code meets standards with a brief summary.

Structure your response for maximum actionability - developers should know exactly what to fix and why.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. 1	# wordstat: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `wordstat/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`).
7	- **Entry point:** `python -m wordstat ...` run from repo root.
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1** `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0.
12	- **R2** `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` reads exactly one file, decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`). stdin is never read.
13	- **R3** Counts, computed on the decoded text:
14	  - `lines` = `len(text.splitlines())`
15	  - `words` = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`
16	  - `chars` = `len(text)` (code points, BOM excluded)
17	- **R4** `top` lists the `N` most frequent words (same tokens as R3), ordered by count descending, then word ascending. `--top` defaults to 3. Fewer than `N` distinct words lists all of them.
18	- **R5** Default output is the text format; `--json` selects the JSON format.
19	- **R6** Output is deterministic: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
20	
21	## Interface contract
22	
23	### Command
24	
25	```
26	python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE
27	```
28	
29	- argparse `prog` is `wordstat`.
30	- `--top` must be an integer >= 1, else usage error.
31	
32	### Text format
33	
34	Exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
35	
36	```
37	lines: <lines>
38	words: <words>
39	chars: <chars>
40	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
41	```
42	
43	With no words, the last line is `top:` with no trailing space.
44	
45	### JSON format
46	
47	One line: the result of `json.dumps(obj)` with default separators, followed by `\n`, where `obj` has keys in this order:
48	
49	```
50	{"lines": <int>, "words": <int>, "chars": <int>, "top": [{"word": <str>, "count": <int>}, ...]}
51	```
52	
53	### Exit codes and errors
54	
55	Errors print one line to stderr, prefix `wordstat: error: `, and leave stdout empty. `<path>` is the FILE argument exactly as given.
56	
57	| Condition | Exit | stderr (after prefix) |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| File missing, a directory, or unreadable | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` |
60	| Not valid UTF-8 | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` |
61	| Usage error (missing FILE, unknown flag, bad `--top`) | 2 | argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: ` |
62	
63	Exit 0 on success, including an empty file. Exit 1 is reserved for unexpected internal errors.
64	
65	## Example
66	
67	`sample.txt` (UTF-8, `\n` endings):
68	
69	```
70	The cat sat.
71	The cat ran!
72	A dog.
73	```
74	
75	`python -m wordstat sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
76	
77	```
78	lines: 3
79	words: 8
80	chars: 33
81	top: cat=2 the=2 a=1
82	```
83	
84	`python -m wordstat --json --top 2 sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
85	
86	```
87	{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}
88	```
89

1	# wordstat Specification
2	
3	**Status:** Planned — see `implementation-plan.md` (3 phases / 4 tasks)
4	**Dependencies:** none (greenfield)
5	**Layer:** Domain (CLI tool)
6	**Priority:** Critical Path (sole feature of this repository)
7	**Estimated Complexity:** 3 phases / 4 tasks
8	
9	**Authoritative source:** [`contract.md`](../../contract.md) at the repository root. This specification
10	elaborates, resolves and documents the contract; it never overrides it. Where this document and
11	`contract.md` appear to differ, `contract.md` wins and the difference must be treated as a defect in
12	this document.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Executive Summary
17	
18	Build `wordstat`, a tiny Python ≥3.11 command-line tool that reads exactly one UTF-8 text file and
19	prints its line, word and character counts plus its `N` most frequent words. The tool runs as
20	`python -m wordstat FILE` from the repository root, uses only the standard library at runtime
21	(pytest for tests only), emits a four-line text summary by default or a single JSON line with
22	`--json`, and behaves byte-for-byte identically on Windows, macOS and Linux. Bad input fails
23	cleanly: one line on stderr with the `wordstat: error: ` prefix, an empty stdout, a specific exit
24	code, and never a traceback.
25	
26	## 2. Problem Statement
27	
28	### Current State
29	
30	The repository contains only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore`. There is no code, no
31	`docs/`, no test infrastructure and no packaging configuration. The contract fully specifies the
32	interface, counting semantics, output formats, exit codes and a worked example.
33	
34	### Impact of Inaction
35	
36	Without the tool there is no way to obtain deterministic word statistics from a text file in this
37	repository; the brief's acceptance example cannot be demonstrated.
38	
39	## 3. Goals & Non-Goals
40	
41	### Goals
42	
43	- G1. Satisfy every requirement in `contract.md` (R1–R6, the interface contract, the exit-code
44	  matrix, the worked example) byte-for-byte.
45	- G2. Provide pytest tests covering the full contract (required by `brief.md`).
46	- G3. Deterministic output on Windows, macOS and Linux: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use.
47	- G4. Clean failure for every bad-input class: exact stderr message, exact exit code, empty
48	  stdout, no traceback.
49	
50	### Non-Goals
51	
52	- NG1. No packaging/distribution (`pyproject.toml`, console scripts, PyPI). The contract fixes
53	  `python -m wordstat` from the repo root only.
54	- NG2. No reading from stdin (R2: stdin is never read), no multiple-file input, no directories
55	  walked recursively.
56	- NG3. No locale-aware or Unicode-aware word segmentation (e.g. no jieba, no `regex` module): the
57	  token is exactly the contract's ASCII regex `[a-z0-9]+` over `text.lower()`.
58	- NG4. No committed `sample.txt` at the repository root; tests materialise the contract's sample
59	  in `tmp_path`.
60	- NG5. No colour/styling, no config files, no `--version`, no progress output.
61	- NG6. No modification of `contract.md` or `brief.md`.
62	
63	## 4. Architecture
64	
65	Flat layout at the repository root (contract: package location, no `src/`):
66	
67	```
68	wordstat/
69	  __init__.py      # package marker; may re-export main for convenience
70	  __main__.py      # thin shim: sys.exit(main())  — executed by `python -m wordstat`
71	  cli.py           # argparse parser, main(), read/count/format logic
72	tests/
73	  test_*.py        # pytest suite (may be split across files)
74	conftest.py        # empty, at repo root — puts the repo root on sys.path for pytest
75	```
76	
77	**Data flow:**
78	
79	```
80	sys.argv → argparse (prog="wordstat")
81	        → read FILE as utf-8-sig (newline="")
82	        → counts: lines / words / chars   (contract R3, literal formulas)
83	        → top-N ranking                   (contract R4, key (-count, word))
84	        → format: text (4 lines) or JSON (1 line)
85	        → single write to reconfigured stdout, flush
86	        → exit 0
87	```
88	
89	**Module responsibilities:**
90	
91	- `__main__.py`: nothing but `from wordstat.cli import main` + `sys.exit(main())`, per the official
92	  `python -m` guidance — keeps argparse/`reconfigure` side effects out of import time and makes
93	  `cli.main()` unit-testable in-process.
94	- `cli.py`:
95	  - `build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser` with `prog="wordstat"`.
96	  - `count(text: str) -> dict` (pure function: lines/words/chars/top).
97	  - `format_text(result) -> str` / `format_json(result) -> str` (pure functions).
98	  - `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` — I/O, error mapping, exit codes.
99	- `tests/`: subprocess-driven end-to-end contract tests (authoritative) plus in-process unit tests
100	  of the pure functions.
101	
102	**Startup sequence inside `main()` (order is normative):**
103	
104	1. `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` and
105	   `sys.stderr.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` — **before any output**, so that
106	   `--help`, argparse usage errors and error messages are all UTF-8/`\n` too.
107	2. Build parser, `parse_args()` (argparse `SystemExit` propagates as-is → exit 2 path).
108	3. Read + decode the file inside `try`/`except` (see §5.4).
109	4. Compute counts and format the entire output string.
110	5. Write the whole string in one call, then flush.
111	6. Return `0`.
112	
113	## 5. Detailed Design
114	
115	### 5.1 Command-line interface (contract: "Command")
116	
117	- `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE`
118	- `ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat")` — **explicit `prog` is mandatory**: under `python -m`,
119	  argparse's default prog is `__main__.py` (verified on this box), which would break the contract's
120	  `^wordstat: error: ` requirement.
121	- `--json`: store-true flag (R5).
122	- `--top N`: custom `type=` callable that parses with `int()` and raises
123	  `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` unless the value is `>= 1`. Plain `type=int` is **not** acceptable —
124	  it accepts `0` and `-1`, violating C2. Non-integer strings must also raise
125	  `ArgumentTypeError`. Exact message wording is not normative; exit code 2 and the stderr prefix
126	  are.
127	- One positional `file` (a single `file` argument name; metavar may be `FILE`). A second positional
128	  or an unknown flag → argparse error → exit 2 (R2 "exactly one file").
129	- `--help` → argparse prints usage/help to **stdout**, exit 0 (R1). Help text content is not
130	  normative beyond that.
131	- **Use argparse's default `error()`** — do not subclass/override it. The contract explicitly asks
132	  for "argparse default", and with `prog="wordstat"` the default already emits the usage block
133	  followed by a final line `wordstat: error: …` and exits 2 (verified).
134	
135	### 5.2 Input reading (contract R2)
136	
137	```python
138	with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
139	    text = f.read()
140	```
141	
142	- `utf-8-sig` strips an optional leading BOM at decode time, so U+FEFF never enters `text` and is
143	  excluded from `chars`; an absent BOM is not an error; a U+FEFF later in the file is a normal
144	  character.
145	- `newline=""` is **decision D1** (see §6) — no newline translation; `text` is exactly the decoded
146	  bytes.
147	- `path` is the FILE argument **exactly as given** (never absolutised) for error messages.
148	- stdin is never opened or read.
149	
150	### 5.3 Counting and ranking (contract R3, R4) — literal formulas
151	
152	```python
153	lines = len(text.splitlines())
154	words = len(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))
155	chars = len(text)                                    # code points, BOM already stripped
156	counts = Counter(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))   # same token stream as `words`
157	top = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:n]
158	```
159	
160	Semantics pinned by research (verified on Python 3.13; stable across 3.11–3.13):
161	
162	- `splitlines()` splits on LF, CR, CRLF (one break), VT, FF, FS, GS, RS, NEL (U+0085), LS
163	  (U+2028), PS (U+2029). A **trailing** line break does not create a final empty line
164	  (`"a\n"` → 1 line; `""` → 0 lines); an interior blank line does count.
165	- `chars = len(text)` counts **code points**, not bytes; astral characters count 1.
166	- The regex runs over `text.lower()` **first** (order matters). `[a-z0-9]` is ASCII-only even
167	  though `re` is Unicode-by-default — a literal range is unaffected by Unicode mode. Therefore
168	  tokens are always lowercase ASCII: `"café"` → `caf`; Cyrillic/CJK/emoji never match but do count
169	  in `chars`.
170	- Do **not** use `re.IGNORECASE` (it would widen the class with `İ ı ſ K`) and do **not** use
171	  `Counter.most_common()` for R4 — its ties are first-seen insertion order, not word-ascending
172	  (verified: `most_common` on `{b:2,a:2,c:1}` → `b,a,c`; explicit `(-count, word)` → `a,b,c`).
173	  The explicit `sorted` key is a total order on distinct tokens ⇒ fully deterministic.
174	- `--top` default is 3; if fewer than `N` distinct words exist, list all of them.
175	
176	### 5.4 Errors and exit codes (contract: "Exit codes and errors")
177	
178	One helper guarantees format discipline:
179	
180	```python
181	def fail(msg: str, code: int) -> int:
182	    print(f"wordstat: error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
183	    return code
184	```
185	
186	| Condition | Detection | Exit | stderr (after prefix) |
187	|---|---|---|---|
188	| Missing file, directory, unreadable | `except OSError` around open/read (`FileNotFoundError`, `IsADirectoryError`, `PermissionError` all subclass `OSError`) | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` |
189	| Not valid UTF-8 | `except UnicodeDecodeError` — **a `ValueError`, not an `OSError`**; must be its own clause, ordered before any broad handler | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` |
190	| Usage error | argparse (missing FILE, unknown flag, bad `--top`, extra positional) | 2 | argparse default; last line matches `^wordstat: error: ` |
191	| Unexpected internal error | `except Exception` catch-all around compute/format/write | 1 | `wordstat: error: <brief description>` (**decision D3**) |
192	| Broken pipe (stdout consumer exits early) | `BrokenPipeError` on write/flush → redirect stdout to devnull, then the exit-1 path (**decision D4**) | 1 | `wordstat: error: broken pipe` |
193	| Success (incl. empty file) | — | 0 | — |
194	
195	Rules:
196	
197	- All reading, decoding, counting and formatting complete **before any stdout write**, so every
198	  error path leaves stdout **empty**.
199	- Exactly one line on stderr for exit 1/3 paths (no usage block); usage errors keep argparse's
200	  usage block with the `wordstat: error: ` line last.
201	- Never raise an uncaught exception out of `main()` — no tracebacks, ever (brief).
202	- Precedence when both could apply: read errors are raised before decoding, so a file that cannot
203	  be read reports `cannot read file`; only a successfully read file can report `not valid UTF-8`.
204	
205	### 5.5 Output formats (contract R5, R6)
206	
207	Both formats are built as **one string** and written with a single `sys.stdout.write(...)` +
208	`sys.stdout.flush()`.
209	
210	**Text (default)** — exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
211	
212	```
213	lines: <lines>\n
214	words: <words>\n
215	chars: <chars>\n
216	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> …\n
217	```
218	
219	- The `top:` pairs are joined by a single space; the line therefore never ends with a trailing
220	  space — with zero words it is exactly `top:\n` (**decision D5**, generalising the contract's
221	  explicit no-trailing-space rule for the empty case).
222	
223	**JSON (`--json`)** — one line:
224	
225	```python
226	json.dumps({"lines": …, "words": …, "chars": …, "top": [{"word": …, "count": …}, …]}) + "\n"
227	```
228	
229	- `json.dumps(obj)` with **no keyword arguments** (default separators `', '` / `': '`,
230	  `ensure_ascii=True`, `indent=None`).
231	- Dict insertion order fixes the key order `lines, words, chars, top`; nested dicts are
232	  `{"word": …, "count": …}` (Python ≥3.7 preserves insertion order).
233	- Output is pure ASCII by construction (tokens are `[a-z0-9]+`), so byte output is identical
234	  under any `ensure_ascii` value — the default is kept for fidelity.
235	
236	**Determinism (R6):** stdout **and stderr** reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"` at
237	startup — this is the only portable fix for Windows CRLF translation of `\n` (default
238	`newline=None` translates on write) and for locale/ANSI-codepage encoding of redirected streams.
239	No `locale` module use, no `os.linesep`, no platform branches anywhere in the code.
240	
241	### 5.6 Environment preconditions (verified 2026-10-25)
242	
243	- Python 3.13.17 ≥ 3.11 ✓; pytest 9.1.1 importable ✓; `sys.stdout.encoding` = `utf-8`,
244	  `LANG`/`LC_ALL` unset — ambient defaults are UTF-8 here, so tests must not rely on that: the
245	  reconfiguration (R6) is what guarantees determinism, and subprocess tests compare raw **bytes**.
246	- Running as **root** (`euid == 0`): `chmod 000` "unreadable file" tests would still open
247	  successfully — permission-denied tests are `skipif(euid == 0)` (**decision D6**); missing-file
248	  and directory cases are the primary exit-3 coverage.

250	## 6. Research Decisions (disagreements & ambiguities resolved)
251	
252	`contract.md` is authoritative; research supports it. Decisions use the contract wording plus
253	empirical evidence; each records the considered alternative.
254	
255	| # | Question | Decision | Alternative (rejected) | Reason |
256	|---|---|---|---|---|
257	| D1 | `open()` `newline=` for reading — changes `chars` for CR/CRLF input | **`newline=""`** (no translation; `text` is the pure `utf-8-sig` decode) | `newline=None` (universal newlines: `\r\n`/`\r` → `\n`, shrinking `chars`) | R2/R3 say counts are computed on "the decoded text" and name only the codec (`utf-8-sig`); universal-newline translation is an extra, contract-silent transform. Verified: bytes `"a\r\nb"` → `chars=4` with `newline=""`, `chars=3` with default. The contract's sample uses `\n` only, so neither choice is observable there; `newline=""` is the literal reading. Deterministic on all platforms either way (translation is platform-independent). |
258	| D2 | argparse usage-error mechanism | **Use argparse's default `error()`**; set only `prog="wordstat"` | Custom `ArgumentParser.error()` subclass (one researcher's recommendation) | The contract says "argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: `". The default, with explicit `prog`, was verified to satisfy both halves; an override risks losing the usage block for no benefit. |
259	| D3 | Exit-1 message format (contract reserves exit 1 but specifies no message) | Single stderr line `wordstat: error: <brief description>`, stdout empty, exit 1 | Silent exit 1 / raw traceback | The "Exit codes and errors" section states errors print one line with the prefix; the brief forbids tracebacks. Applying the general error rule to the reserved code is the reading closest to the contract. |
260	| D4 | `BrokenPipeError` (e.g. `| head`) currently produces a traceback and exit 120 | Catch it, silence the broken stdout, exit 1 with `wordstat: error: broken pipe` | Ignore (out of contract scope) | Contract is silent, but the brief demands "never a traceback"; exit 1 is the reserved internal-error slot. Minimal ~4-line guard; recorded as a scope decision in `handoff.md`. |
261	| D5 | Trailing space on a non-empty `top:` line | Pairs joined with single space ⇒ never a trailing space; empty ⇒ exactly `top:` | Allow a trailing space when non-empty | Follows the contract template (`<word>=<count> <word>=<count> …`) plus its explicit empty-case rule; a trailing space only in one branch would be inconsistent. |
262	| D6 | Permission-denied exit-3 test under root | `@pytest.mark.skipif(os.geteuid() == 0)`; rely on missing-file + directory cases | Always run `chmod 000` test | Verified `euid == 0` on this box — root ignores permission bits, so the test would be vacuous/false-failing. |
263	| D7 | `Counter.most_common(N)` for R4 | **Explicit `sorted(key=(-count, word))[:N]`** | `Counter.most_common` | Verified: `most_common` tie order is first-seen insertion order, violating "then word ascending". |
264	
265	Assumptions (explicit, all consistent with the contract):
266	
267	- A1. `python -m wordstat` is only required to work from the repository root; other directories,
268	  `-P`/`PYTHONSAFEPATH`, and installed console scripts are out of scope (contract fixes the entry
269	  point).
270	- A2. Help/usage text wording beyond the `prog` name and exit codes is not normative.
271	- A3. Two files → one `file` positional → argparse "unrecognized arguments" → exit 2; the contract
272	  implies this via "reads exactly one file".
273	- A4. Exit-code matrix is closed: 0 success, 1 internal, 2 usage, 3 read/decode — no other codes.
274	- A5. Tests run as `python -m pytest` or bare `pytest` from the repository root; the root
275	  `conftest.py` makes `import wordstat` work either way.

286	## 8. Risks & Mitigations
287	
288	| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
289	|---|---|---|
290	| Forgetting explicit `prog="wordstat"` | Every usage error reads `__main__.py: error: …` → contract violation | Test asserts last stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: ` (not `__main__.py`) |
291	| `type=int` for `--top` | `--top 0`/`-1` accepted → contract violation | Custom type raising `ArgumentTypeError`; tests for `0`, `-1`, `abc` |
292	| `UnicodeDecodeError` caught under `OSError` | Invalid UTF-8 misreported as `cannot read file` | Separate `except UnicodeDecodeError` clause, ordered first |
293	| `Counter.most_common` used for ties | Wrong tie order on equal counts | Explicit `(-count, word)` sort; tie test (`cat=2 the=2`) |
294	| CRLF/Windows `\r\n` on stdout | Byte output differs across OSes | `reconfigure(newline="\n")` + byte-level subprocess assertions |
295	| Writing output before an error occurs | Non-empty stdout on error paths | Compute/format everything before the single write; `stdout == b""` asserted on every error test |
296	| Permission tests under root (euid 0) | Vacuous or failing test | `skipif(euid == 0)`; primary exit-3 cases are missing file + directory |
297	| Traceback escaping `main()` | Brief violation | Top-level `except Exception` → exit 1; `BrokenPipeError` guard |
298	| In-process tests missing the reconfigure path | False confidence in determinism | Subprocess tests (`sys.executable -m wordstat`, `cwd=repo_root`) are authoritative for all byte/exit-code assertions |

1	# wordstat Specification
2	
3	**Status:** Planned — see `implementation-plan.md` (3 phases / 4 tasks)
4	**Dependencies:** none (greenfield)
5	**Layer:** Domain (CLI tool)
6	**Priority:** Critical Path (sole feature of this repository)
7	**Estimated Complexity:** 3 phases / 4 tasks
8	
9	**Authoritative source:** [`contract.md`](../../contract.md) at the repository root. This specification
10	elaborates, resolves and documents the contract; it never overrides it. Where this document and
11	`contract.md` appear to differ, `contract.md` wins and the difference must be treated as a defect in
12	this document.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Executive Summary
17	
18	Build `wordstat`, a tiny Python ≥3.11 command-line tool that reads exactly one UTF-8 text file and
19	prints its line, word and character counts plus its `N` most frequent words. The tool runs as
20	`python -m wordstat FILE` from the repository root, uses only the standard library at runtime
21	(pytest for tests only), emits a four-line text summary by default or a single JSON line with
22	`--json`, and behaves byte-for-byte identically on Windows, macOS and Linux. Bad input fails
23	cleanly: one line on stderr with the `wordstat: error: ` prefix, an empty stdout, a specific exit
24	code, and never a traceback.
25	
26	## 2. Problem Statement
27	
28	### Current State
29	
30	The repository contains only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore`. There is no code, no
31	`docs/`, no test infrastructure and no packaging configuration. The contract fully specifies the
32	interface, counting semantics, output formats, exit codes and a worked example.
33	
34	### Impact of Inaction
35	
36	Without the tool there is no way to obtain deterministic word statistics from a text file in this
37	repository; the brief's acceptance example cannot be demonstrated.
38	
39	## 3. Goals & Non-Goals
40	
41	### Goals
42	
43	- G1. Satisfy every requirement in `contract.md` (R1–R6, the interface contract, the exit-code
44	  matrix, the worked example) byte-for-byte.
45	- G2. Provide pytest tests covering the full contract (required by `brief.md`).
46	- G3. Deterministic output on Windows, macOS and Linux: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use.
47	- G4. Clean failure for every bad-input class: exact stderr message, exact exit code, empty
48	  stdout, no traceback.
49	
50	### Non-Goals
51	
52	- NG1. No packaging/distribution (`pyproject.toml`, console scripts, PyPI). The contract fixes
53	  `python -m wordstat` from the repo root only.
54	- NG2. No reading from stdin (R2: stdin is never read), no multiple-file input, no directories
55	  walked recursively.
56	- NG3. No locale-aware or Unicode-aware word segmentation (e.g. no jieba, no `regex` module): the
57	  token is exactly the contract's ASCII regex `[a-z0-9]+` over `text.lower()`.
58	- NG4. No committed `sample.txt` at the repository root; tests materialise the contract's sample
59	  in `tmp_path`.
60	- NG5. No colour/styling, no config files, no `--version`, no progress output.
61	- NG6. No modification of `contract.md` or `brief.md`.
62	
63	## 4. Architecture
64	
65	Flat layout at the repository root (contract: package location, no `src/`):
66	
67	```
68	wordstat/
69	  __init__.py      # package marker; may re-export main for convenience
70	  __main__.py      # thin shim: sys.exit(main())  — executed by `python -m wordstat`
71	  cli.py           # argparse parser, main(), read/count/format logic
72	tests/
73	  test_*.py        # pytest suite (may be split across files)
74	conftest.py        # empty, at repo root — puts the repo root on sys.path for pytest
75	```
76	
77	**Data flow:**
78	
79	```
80	sys.argv → argparse (prog="wordstat")
81	        → read FILE as utf-8-sig (newline="")
82	        → counts: lines / words / chars   (contract R3, literal formulas)
83	        → top-N ranking                   (contract R4, key (-count, word))
84	        → format: text (4 lines) or JSON (1 line)
85	        → single write to reconfigured stdout, flush
86	        → exit 0
87	```
88	
89	**Module responsibilities:**
90	
91	- `__main__.py`: nothing but `from wordstat.cli import main` + `sys.exit(main())`, per the official
92	  `python -m` guidance — keeps argparse/`reconfigure` side effects out of import time and makes
93	  `cli.main()` unit-testable in-process.
94	- `cli.py`:
95	  - `build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser` with `prog="wordstat"`.
96	  - `count(text: str) -> dict` (pure function: lines/words/chars/top).
97	  - `format_text(result) -> str` / `format_json(result) -> str` (pure functions).
98	  - `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` — I/O, error mapping, exit codes.
99	- `tests/`: subprocess-driven end-to-end contract tests (authoritative) plus in-process unit tests
100	  of the pure functions.
101	
102	**Startup sequence inside `main()` (order is normative):**
103	
104	1. `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` and
105	   `sys.stderr.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` — **before any output**, so that
106	   `--help`, argparse usage errors and error messages are all UTF-8/`\n` too.
107	2. Build parser, `parse_args()` (argparse `SystemExit` propagates as-is → exit 2 path).
108	3. Read + decode the file inside `try`/`except` (see §5.4).
109	4. Compute counts and format the entire output string.
110	5. Write the whole string in one call, then flush.
111	6. Return `0`.
112	
113	## 5. Detailed Design
114	
115	### 5.1 Command-line interface (contract: "Command")
116	
117	- `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE`
118	- `ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat")` — **explicit `prog` is mandatory**: under `python -m`,
119	  argparse's default prog is `__main__.py` (verified on this box), which would break the contract's
120	  `^wordstat: error: ` requirement.
121	- `--json`: store-true flag (R5).
122	- `--top N`: custom `type=` callable that parses with `int()` and raises
123	  `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` unless the value is `>= 1`. Plain `type=int` is **not** acceptable —
124	  it accepts `0` and `-1`, violating C2. Non-integer strings must also raise
125	  `ArgumentTypeError`. Exact message wording is not normative; exit code 2 and the stderr prefix
126	  are.
127	- One positional `file` (a single `file` argument name; metavar may be `FILE`). A second positional
128	  or an unknown flag → argparse error → exit 2 (R2 "exactly one file").
129	- `--help` → argparse prints usage/help to **stdout**, exit 0 (R1). Help text content is not
130	  normative beyond that.
131	- **Use argparse's default `error()`** — do not subclass/override it. The contract explicitly asks
132	  for "argparse default", and with `prog="wordstat"` the default already emits the usage block
133	  followed by a final line `wordstat: error: …` and exits 2 (verified).
134	
135	### 5.2 Input reading (contract R2)
136	
137	```python
138	with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
139	    text = f.read()
140	```
141	
142	- `utf-8-sig` strips an optional leading BOM at decode time, so U+FEFF never enters `text` and is
143	  excluded from `chars`; an absent BOM is not an error; a U+FEFF later in the file is a normal
144	  character.
145	- `newline=""` is **decision D1** (see §6) — no newline translation; `text` is exactly the decoded
146	  bytes.
147	- `path` is the FILE argument **exactly as given** (never absolutised) for error messages.
148	- stdin is never opened or read.
149	
150	### 5.3 Counting and ranking (contract R3, R4) — literal formulas
151	
152	```python
153	lines = len(text.splitlines())
154	words = len(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))
155	chars = len(text)                                    # code points, BOM already stripped
156	counts = Counter(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))   # same token stream as `words`
157	top = sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:n]
158	```
159	
160	Semantics pinned by research (verified on Python 3.13; stable across 3.11–3.13):
161	
162	- `splitlines()` splits on LF, CR, CRLF (one break), VT, FF, FS, GS, RS, NEL (U+0085), LS
163	  (U+2028), PS (U+2029). A **trailing** line break does not create a final empty line
164	  (`"a\n"` → 1 line; `""` → 0 lines); an interior blank line does count.
165	- `chars = len(text)` counts **code points**, not bytes; astral characters count 1.
166	- The regex runs over `text.lower()` **first** (order matters). `[a-z0-9]` is ASCII-only even
167	  though `re` is Unicode-by-default — a literal range is unaffected by Unicode mode. Therefore
168	  tokens are always lowercase ASCII: `"café"` → `caf`; Cyrillic/CJK/emoji never match but do count
169	  in `chars`.
170	- Do **not** use `re.IGNORECASE` (it would widen the class with `İ ı ſ K`) and do **not** use
171	  `Counter.most_common()` for R4 — its ties are first-seen insertion order, not word-ascending
172	  (verified: `most_common` on `{b:2,a:2,c:1}` → `b,a,c`; explicit `(-count, word)` → `a,b,c`).
173	  The explicit `sorted` key is a total order on distinct tokens ⇒ fully deterministic.
174	- `--top` default is 3; if fewer than `N` distinct words exist, list all of them.
175	
176	### 5.4 Errors and exit codes (contract: "Exit codes and errors")
177	
178	One helper guarantees format discipline:
179	
180	```python
181	def fail(msg: str, code: int) -> int:
182	    print(f"wordstat: error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
183	    return code
184	```
185	
186	| Condition | Detection | Exit | stderr (after prefix) |
187	|---|---|---|---|
188	| Missing file, directory, unreadable | `except OSError` around open/read (`FileNotFoundError`, `IsADirectoryError`, `PermissionError` all subclass `OSError`) | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` |
189	| Not valid UTF-8 | `except UnicodeDecodeError` — **a `ValueError`, not an `OSError`**; must be its own clause, ordered before any broad handler | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` |
190	| Usage error | argparse (missing FILE, unknown flag, bad `--top`, extra positional) | 2 | argparse default; last line matches `^wordstat: error: ` |
191	| Unexpected internal error | `except Exception` catch-all around compute/format/write | 1 | `wordstat: error: <brief description>` (**decision D3**) |
192	| Broken pipe (stdout consumer exits early) | `BrokenPipeError` on write/flush → redirect stdout to devnull, then the exit-1 path (**decision D4**) | 1 | `wordstat: error: broken pipe` |
193	| Success (incl. empty file) | — | 0 | — |
194	
195	Rules:
196	
197	- All reading, decoding, counting and formatting complete **before any stdout write**, so every
198	  error path leaves stdout **empty**.
199	- Exactly one line on stderr for exit 1/3 paths (no usage block); usage errors keep argparse's
200	  usage block with the `wordstat: error: ` line last.
201	- Never raise an uncaught exception out of `main()` — no tracebacks, ever (brief).
202	- Precedence when both could apply: read errors are raised before decoding, so a file that cannot
203	  be read reports `cannot read file`; only a successfully read file can report `not valid UTF-8`.
204	
205	### 5.5 Output formats (contract R5, R6)
206	
207	Both formats are built as **one string** and written with a single `sys.stdout.write(...)` +
208	`sys.stdout.flush()`.
209	
210	**Text (default)** — exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
211	
212	```
213	lines: <lines>\n
214	words: <words>\n
215	chars: <chars>\n
216	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> …\n
217	```
218	
219	- The `top:` pairs are joined by a single space; the line therefore never ends with a trailing
220	  space — with zero words it is exactly `top:\n` (**decision D5**, generalising the contract's
221	  explicit no-trailing-space rule for the empty case).
222	
223	**JSON (`--json`)** — one line:
224	
225	```python
226	json.dumps({"lines": …, "words": …, "chars": …, "top": [{"word": …, "count": …}, …]}) + "\n"
227	```
228	
229	- `json.dumps(obj)` with **no keyword arguments** (default separators `', '` / `': '`,
230	  `ensure_ascii=True`, `indent=None`).
231	- Dict insertion order fixes the key order `lines, words, chars, top`; nested dicts are
232	  `{"word": …, "count": …}` (Python ≥3.7 preserves insertion order).
233	- Output is pure ASCII by construction (tokens are `[a-z0-9]+`), so byte output is identical
234	  under any `ensure_ascii` value — the default is kept for fidelity.
235	
236	**Determinism (R6):** stdout **and stderr** reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"` at
237	startup — this is the only portable fix for Windows CRLF translation of `\n` (default
238	`newline=None` translates on write) and for locale/ANSI-codepage encoding of redirected streams.
239	No `locale` module use, no `os.linesep`, no platform branches anywhere in the code.
240	
241	### 5.6 Environment preconditions (verified 2026-10-25)
242	
243	- Python 3.13.17 ≥ 3.11 ✓; pytest 9.1.1 importable ✓; `sys.stdout.encoding` = `utf-8`,
244	  `LANG`/`LC_ALL` unset — ambient defaults are UTF-8 here, so tests must not rely on that: the
245	  reconfiguration (R6) is what guarantees determinism, and subprocess tests compare raw **bytes**.
246	- Running as **root** (`euid == 0`): `chmod 000` "unreadable file" tests would still open
247	  successfully — permission-denied tests are `skipif(euid == 0)` (**decision D6**); missing-file
248	  and directory cases are the primary exit-3 coverage.
249	
250	## 6. Research Decisions (disagreements & ambiguities resolved)
251	
252	`contract.md` is authoritative; research supports it. Decisions use the contract wording plus
253	empirical evidence; each records the considered alternative.
254	
255	| # | Question | Decision | Alternative (rejected) | Reason |
256	|---|---|---|---|---|
257	| D1 | `open()` `newline=` for reading — changes `chars` for CR/CRLF input | **`newline=""`** (no translation; `text` is the pure `utf-8-sig` decode) | `newline=None` (universal newlines: `\r\n`/`\r` → `\n`, shrinking `chars`) | R2/R3 say counts are computed on "the decoded text" and name only the codec (`utf-8-sig`); universal-newline translation is an extra, contract-silent transform. Verified: bytes `"a\r\nb"` → `chars=4` with `newline=""`, `chars=3` with default. The contract's sample uses `\n` only, so neither choice is observable there; `newline=""` is the literal reading. Deterministic on all platforms either way (translation is platform-independent). |
258	| D2 | argparse usage-error mechanism | **Use argparse's default `error()`**; set only `prog="wordstat"` | Custom `ArgumentParser.error()` subclass (one researcher's recommendation) | The contract says "argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: `". The default, with explicit `prog`, was verified to satisfy both halves; an override risks losing the usage block for no benefit. |
259	| D3 | Exit-1 message format (contract reserves exit 1 but specifies no message) | Single stderr line `wordstat: error: <brief description>`, stdout empty, exit 1 | Silent exit 1 / raw traceback | The "Exit codes and errors" section states errors print one line with the prefix; the brief forbids tracebacks. Applying the general error rule to the reserved code is the reading closest to the contract. |
260	| D4 | `BrokenPipeError` (e.g. `| head`) currently produces a traceback and exit 120 | Catch it, silence the broken stdout, exit 1 with `wordstat: error: broken pipe` | Ignore (out of contract scope) | Contract is silent, but the brief demands "never a traceback"; exit 1 is the reserved internal-error slot. Minimal ~4-line guard; recorded as a scope decision in `handoff.md`. |
261	| D5 | Trailing space on a non-empty `top:` line | Pairs joined with single space ⇒ never a trailing space; empty ⇒ exactly `top:` | Allow a trailing space when non-empty | Follows the contract template (`<word>=<count> <word>=<count> …`) plus its explicit empty-case rule; a trailing space only in one branch would be inconsistent. |
262	| D6 | Permission-denied exit-3 test under root | `@pytest.mark.skipif(os.geteuid() == 0)`; rely on missing-file + directory cases | Always run `chmod 000` test | Verified `euid == 0` on this box — root ignores permission bits, so the test would be vacuous/false-failing. |
263	| D7 | `Counter.most_common(N)` for R4 | **Explicit `sorted(key=(-count, word))[:N]`** | `Counter.most_common` | Verified: `most_common` tie order is first-seen insertion order, violating "then word ascending". |
264	
265	Assumptions (explicit, all consistent with the contract):
266	
267	- A1. `python -m wordstat` is only required to work from the repository root; other directories,
268	  `-P`/`PYTHONSAFEPATH`, and installed console scripts are out of scope (contract fixes the entry
269	  point).
270	- A2. Help/usage text wording beyond the `prog` name and exit codes is not normative.
271	- A3. Two files → one `file` positional → argparse "unrecognized arguments" → exit 2; the contract
272	  implies this via "reads exactly one file".
273	- A4. Exit-code matrix is closed: 0 success, 1 internal, 2 usage, 3 read/decode — no other codes.
274	- A5. Tests run as `python -m pytest` or bare `pytest` from the repository root; the root
275	  `conftest.py` makes `import wordstat` work either way.
276	
277	## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)
278	
279	High-level only — `/geeky-plan` produces the normative task breakdown and kanban.
280	
281	1. **Phase A — Core package:** `wordstat/` package, parser, counting, ranking, both formatters,
282	   error handling, `__main__` shim, stdout/stderr reconfiguration.
283	2. **Phase B — Tests & verification:** pytest suite per the matrix in §9, root `conftest.py`,
284	   `.gitignore` additions (`.pytest_cache/`), full green run from repo root.
285	
286	## 8. Risks & Mitigations
287	
288	| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
289	|---|---|---|
290	| Forgetting explicit `prog="wordstat"` | Every usage error reads `__main__.py: error: …` → contract violation | Test asserts last stderr line matches `^wordstat: error: ` (not `__main__.py`) |
291	| `type=int` for `--top` | `--top 0`/`-1` accepted → contract violation | Custom type raising `ArgumentTypeError`; tests for `0`, `-1`, `abc` |
292	| `UnicodeDecodeError` caught under `OSError` | Invalid UTF-8 misreported as `cannot read file` | Separate `except UnicodeDecodeError` clause, ordered first |
293	| `Counter.most_common` used for ties | Wrong tie order on equal counts | Explicit `(-count, word)` sort; tie test (`cat=2 the=2`) |
294	| CRLF/Windows `\r\n` on stdout | Byte output differs across OSes | `reconfigure(newline="\n")` + byte-level subprocess assertions |
295	| Writing output before an error occurs | Non-empty stdout on error paths | Compute/format everything before the single write; `stdout == b""` asserted on every error test |
296	| Permission tests under root (euid 0) | Vacuous or failing test | `skipif(euid == 0)`; primary exit-3 cases are missing file + directory |
297	| Traceback escaping `main()` | Brief violation | Top-level `except Exception` → exit 1; `BrokenPipeError` guard |
298	| In-process tests missing the reconfigure path | False confidence in determinism | Subprocess tests (`sys.executable -m wordstat`, `cwd=repo_root`) are authoritative for all byte/exit-code assertions |
299	
300	## 9. Acceptance Criteria
301	
302	Every row is a required test; "exact" means byte-for-byte (`capsys`/`capture_output` **bytes**).
303	
304	| # | Case | Expectation |
305	|---|---|---|
306	| AC1 | `--help` | exit 0; usage/help on stdout; `usage: wordstat` present |
307	| AC2 | Contract sample, default | exit 0; stdout exact `lines: 3\nwords: 8\nchars: 33\ntop: cat=2 the=2 a=1\n` |
308	| AC3 | Contract sample, `--json --top 2` | exit 0; stdout exact `{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}\n` |
309	| AC4 | `--top 1`, `--top` > distinct count | correct truncation / list-all behaviour |
310	| AC5 | Tie ordering | count desc, then word asc (e.g. `cat=2 the=2 a=1`); deterministic across runs |
311	| AC6 | Empty file | exit 0; `lines: 0 words: 0 chars: 0`; last line exactly `top:` (no trailing space); JSON `"top": []` |
312	| AC7 | No-word file (punctuation/whitespace only) | exit 0; words 0; `top:` |
313	| AC8 | UTF-8 BOM present | BOM stripped; `chars` excludes it; identical output to same file without BOM |
314	| AC9 | CRLF file | `lines`/`words` correct per `splitlines()`; `chars` includes `\r` (D1); LF-only twin differs only in `chars` |
315	| AC10 | No trailing newline | same `lines` as the version with one |
316	| AC11 | Missing FILE argument | exit 2; last stderr line `^wordstat: error: `; stdout empty |
317	| AC12 | Unknown flag | exit 2; same stderr/stdout rules |
318	| AC13 | `--top 0`, `--top -1`, `--top abc`, `--top` (no value) | exit 2; same stderr/stdout rules |
319	| AC14 | Missing file | exit 3; stderr exact `wordstat: error: <path>: cannot read file\n`; stdout empty |
320	| AC15 | Directory as FILE | exit 3; `… cannot read file`; stdout empty |
321	| AC16 | Invalid UTF-8 bytes | exit 3; stderr exact `wordstat: error: <path>: not valid UTF-8\n`; stdout empty |
322	| AC17 | Two positional FILEs | exit 2; stdout empty |
323	| AC18 | Empty stdout on **every** error path | `r.stdout == b""` |

1	# wordstat — Implementation Plan
2	
3	**Feature folder:** `docs/spec-001-feature/`
4	**Authoritative requirement:** [`contract.md`](../../contract.md) (repo root) — never modified by this plan.
5	**Specification:** [`feature-specification.md`](feature-specification.md) (elaborates the contract; §6 decisions D1–D7 are binding on implementation).
6	**Brief:** [`brief.md`](../../brief.md) — adds the pytest-tests and never-a-traceback requirements.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 1. Overview
11	
12	Deliver `wordstat`, a standard-library-only Python ≥3.11 CLI (`python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE`
13	from the repo root) that prints line/word/char counts plus top-N words, byte-for-byte deterministically,
14	with an exact exit-code matrix and single-line prefixed stderr errors.
15	
16	**Definition of done for the whole plan:** the full pytest suite is green from the repository root and
17	every acceptance criterion AC1–AC22 in `feature-specification.md` §9 has a passing test as evidence.
18	
19	### Binding design decisions (from spec §6 — do not re-litigate)
20	
21	| ID | Decision |
22	|---|---|
23	| D1 | Read with `open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="")` — no newline translation; `chars` counts CR/CRLF as-is. |
24	| D2 | Use argparse's default `error()`; only set `prog="wordstat"` explicitly. |
25	| D3 | Unexpected internal errors → one stderr line `wordstat: error: <brief description>`, exit 1. |
26	| D4 | `BrokenPipeError` → silence broken stdout (dup2 to devnull), one stderr line, exit 1. |
27	| D5 | `top:` pairs joined by a single space; never a trailing space; empty ⇒ exactly `top:`. |
28	| D6 | Permission-denied test is `skipif(os.geteuid() == 0)`; missing-file + directory are the primary exit-3 cases. |
29	| D7 | Top-N ranking via `sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:n]` — never `Counter.most_common`. |
30	
31	### Target layout (end state)
32	
33	```
34	wordstat/__init__.py        # package marker (may re-export main)
35	wordstat/cli.py             # build_parser, count, format_text, format_json, fail, main
36	wordstat/__main__.py        # sys.exit(main())
37	tests/conftest-see-root     # (root conftest.py, not under tests/)
38	conftest.py                 # empty; puts repo root on sys.path for bare `pytest`
39	tests/test_core.py          # T1 unit tests (pure functions)
40	tests/test_cli.py           # T2 subprocess smoke tests
41	tests/test_contract.py      # T3 contract acceptance matrix
42	tests/test_hardening.py     # T4 determinism/robustness tests
43	docs/spec-001-feature/…     # planning package (this folder)
44	```
45	
46	Runtime imports: standard library only (`argparse`, `json`, `re`, `sys`, `collections`,
47	`os` for devnull/`geteuid` in tests only). `pytest` appears only under `tests/`.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Implementation phases
52	
53	Phases are review batches: members of a phase share one phase review; the phase advances only on
54	READY TO ADVANCE. Tasks run strictly in dependency order.
55	
56	### Phase A — Core implementation (T1, T2)
57	
58	**Goal:** a working, smoke-tested tool that satisfies R1–R6, the command contract, both output
59	formats and the exit-code matrix.
60	
61	- **T1 — Core counting and formatting library.** Pure, side-effect-free logic in
62	  `wordstat/cli.py`: `build_parser()`, `count(text, top)`, `format_text(result)`,
63	  `format_json(result)`; package scaffold (`wordstat/__init__.py`, root `conftest.py`) and
64	  in-process unit tests (`tests/test_core.py`). No file I/O, no `sys.exit`, no output writing.
65	  *Why first:* every later task tests against these exact functions; they encode R3/R4/R5 and
66	  decisions D5/D7 where bugs are cheapest to catch.
67	- **T2 — CLI wiring: I/O, errors, exit codes, entry point.** `main()` with the normative startup
68	  sequence (reconfigure stdout+stderr → parse → read → count → format → single write → flush),
69	  `fail()` helper, `OSError`/`UnicodeDecodeError` mapping (D1 read), D3 catch-all, thin
70	  `wordstat/__main__.py`; subprocess smoke tests (`tests/test_cli.py`): help, contract sample
71	  (both formats), and the five error classes.
72	
73	**Phase A gate:** `python -m pytest tests/test_core.py tests/test_cli.py -q` green; manual
74	contract-example demo from a **temp file** (printf sample → `/tmp` path → `python -m wordstat
75	<tmp-path>`), never a committed `sample.txt` (NG4).
76	
77	### Phase B — Contract coverage (T3)
78	
79	**Goal:** every acceptance criterion AC1–AC22 has a byte-exact test.
80	
81	- **T3 — Contract acceptance suite.** `tests/test_contract.py` — subprocess-driven
82	  (`sys.executable -m wordstat`, `cwd=repo_root`, `capture_output=True` → bytes): byte-exact
83	  worked example, ties, empty/no-word/BOM/CRLF/no-trailing-newline inputs, all usage errors
84	  (incl. two positionals), all exit-3 errors, empty-stdout-on-error, no-traceback, stdin-never-read,
85	  repeated-run determinism. Embeds the contract sample in `tmp_path` (no committed `sample.txt`).
86	
87	**Phase B gate:** `python -m pytest tests/test_contract.py -q` green; full suite green.
88	
89	### Phase C — Hardening, determinism & hygiene (T4)
90	
91	**Goal:** cross-platform determinism proven, robustness complete, repo tidy.
92	
93	- **T4 — Hardening and repo hygiene.** Product: D4 `BrokenPipeError` guard in `main()`.
94	  Tests (`tests/test_hardening.py`): env-variant determinism (`LANG=C`, `LC_ALL=C`,
95	  `PYTHONIOENCODING` set → identical raw stdout bytes), permission-denied test with D6
96	  `skipif(euid == 0)`, `\n`-only byte assertions (AC19). Hygiene: `.gitignore` += `.pytest_cache/`.
97	  Final: full-suite green + contract example demo recorded in notes.
98	
99	**Phase C gate:** `python -m pytest -q` green; then the absolute-path gates from §5
100	(`…/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-kanban.py` and `check-dod.py --task T4`) exit 0.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## 3. Task sequencing and dependencies
105	
106	```
107	T1 (core library + unit tests)
108	 └─► T2 (CLI wiring + smoke tests)
109	      └─► T3 (contract acceptance suite)
110	           └─► T4 (hardening + determinism + hygiene)
111	```
112	
113	Strictly sequential — each task's validation requires the previous task's code. No parallel batches.
114	WIP cap 3 (never reached: at most 1 In Progress).
115	
116	## 4. Testing strategy
117	
118	| Layer | File | Style | Proves |
119	|---|---|---|---|
120	| Unit | `tests/test_core.py` | in-process (`import wordstat.cli`) | R3/R4/R5 formulas, D5/D7, tokenisation edges (`café`, `İ`) |
121	| Smoke | `tests/test_cli.py` | subprocess bytes | R1/R2/R6 wiring, exit codes 0/2/3, prefix, empty stdout |
122	| Contract | `tests/test_contract.py` | subprocess bytes | AC1–AC22 byte-exact evidence |
123	| Hardening | `tests/test_hardening.py` | subprocess bytes + env variants | B2 determinism, AC19, D6, D4 |
124	
125	Rules for all test code:
126	
127	- Assert on **bytes** (`r.stdout`, `r.stderr`), not decoded text — this is what locks `\n` and UTF-8.
128	- Run the tool as `[sys.executable, "-m", "wordstat", *args]` with `cwd=REPO_ROOT`
129	  (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`) — the only invocation mode the contract supports.
130	- Error assertions: `r.returncode`, exact stderr line(s), and `r.stdout == b""`; for exit 2 also
131	  `r.stderr.splitlines()[-1].startswith(b"wordstat: error: ")` and `not r.stderr.startswith(...usage...)`
132	  is NOT asserted (usage block is allowed) — only the last-line rule.
133	- Create every input file in `tmp_path`; never depend on a committed `sample.txt` (NG4).
134	- No test may require network, third-party packages beyond pytest, or non-root permissions to pass
135	  (D6).
136	
137	## 5. Validation gates (run, don't self-report)
138	
139	After each task, before the next starts — exact commands are also in each task file:
140	
141	1. Task validation block (per-task pytest target) exits 0.
142	2. `python "/root/repos/.eval-cfg-20261025T005533Z/plugin/geeky-orchestration/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "docs/spec-001-feature"` after every lane move.
143	3. `…/scripts/check-dod.py --path "docs/spec-001-feature" --task <ID>` before moving to Done
144	   (requires `tasks/<ID>-*.notes.md`, Done-lane placement, handoff mention).
145	4. `…/scripts/check-commit.py --message "<msg>"` before every commit (Conventional Commits
146	   subject ≤72 chars + `Tasks: T<n>` line).
147	5. End of plan: `validate-task-schema.py`, `validate-kanban.py`, `validate-planning-folder.py` all exit 0.
148	6. Start of implement: same three validators re-run; `contract.md`/`brief.md` remain untouched
149	   (verify with `git diff --stat` — only `wordstat/`, `tests/`, `conftest.py`, `.gitignore`,
150	   `docs/spec-001-feature/` may change).
151	7. Stdlib-only spot-check (contract L5 / draft HY3): `grep -hE '^(import|from) ' wordstat/*.py`
152	   lists only standard-library modules; no third-party import (pytest included) appears under
153	   `wordstat/`. Run at the end of T2, T4 and at phase reviews.
154	
155	## 6. Risks (top of mind for implementers)
156	
157	1. **`prog` forgotten** → every usage error reads `__main__.py:`. Guarded by AC11–AC13 tests.
158	2. **`type=int` for `--top`** → `--top 0` accepted. Custom `ArgumentTypeError` type required.
159	3. **`UnicodeDecodeError` under `except OSError`** → wrong message. Separate clause, ordered first.
160	4. **`most_common` used for ties** → wrong order (D7). Tie test AC5 catches it.
161	5. **Output written before an error** → non-empty stdout. Structure `main()` so the single write is last.
162	6. **Windows CRLF / locale encoding** → R6 `reconfigure` on **both** streams, before any output;
163	   proven by env-variant tests in T4 (local runs cannot reproduce Windows, so the guard must be
164	   structural, not platform-tested).
165	7. **Traceback escaping `main()`** → D3 catch-all + D4 pipe guard; AC22 asserts no `Traceback`.
166	
167	## 7. Out of scope (restate)
168	
169	Packaging/console scripts, stdin input, multi-file input, Unicode-aware tokenisation, committed
170	`sample.txt`, colour output, `--version`, any edit to `contract.md`/`brief.md`.

1	Task Name:
2	Build wordstat core library: parser, counting, ranking, formatters
3	
4	Context:
5	Phase A first task. Everything downstream (CLI wiring, contract suite, hardening) tests against the
6	pure functions created here. This task encodes the contract's counting semantics (R3), top-N ranking
7	(R4), both output formats (R5) and the no-trailing-space rule (D5) while bugs are cheapest to catch.
8	No I/O, no `sys.exit` on success paths, no subprocess work — pure logic plus its unit tests.
9	
10	Scope:
11	
12	In scope:
13	---
14	- Create `wordstat/__init__.py` (package marker; may re-export `main` later — plain empty or
15	  docstring-only for now).
16	- Create `wordstat/cli.py` with pure functions only:
17	  - `build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser` — `prog="wordstat"`, `--json` (store_true,
18	    default False), `--top` (custom `type=` callable: `int()` parse, raise
19	    `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` unless `>= 1`; also raise `ArgumentTypeError` on non-integer
20	    input), default `3`, one positional `file`.
21	  - `count(text: str, top: int) -> dict` returning exactly
22	    `{"lines": int, "words": int, "chars": int, "top": list[tuple[str, int]]}` using the literal
23	    contract formulas: `len(text.splitlines())`, `len(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower()))`,
24	    `len(text)`; ranking via `sorted(Counter(...).items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:top]`
25	    (D7 — never `Counter.most_common`).
26	  - `format_text(result: dict) -> str` — the four contract lines, each ending in `\n`, pairs joined
27	    by single space, empty top ⇒ exactly `top:\n` (D5).
28	  - `format_json(result: dict) -> str` — `json.dumps(obj) + "\n"` with default separators, key
29	    order `lines, words, chars, top`, nested keys `word, count`, `top` items built from the
30	    `(word, count)` tuples.
31	- Create root `conftest.py` (empty) so bare `pytest` from the repo root imports `wordstat`
32	  (assumption A5).
33	- Create `tests/test_core.py` — in-process unit tests (import `wordstat.cli` directly).

36	- `main()`, file reading, `sys.stdout` reconfiguration, `fail()`, error-to-exit-code mapping (T2).

49	- Follow `feature-specification.md` §5.3 (counting semantics) and §6 decisions D5/D7; the contract's
50	  worked example (contract.md §Example) is the ground truth: sample text
51	  `"The cat sat.\nThe cat ran!\nA dog.\n"` → lines 3, words 8, chars 33, default top
52	  `[("cat",2), ("the",2), ("a",1)]`.

54	  points → tokens `i`, `stanbul`; never use `re.IGNORECASE`.

56	  can write once (T2 relies on this).

58	  be `__main__.py` (spec §5.1).

60	  `wordstat: error: …` to stderr — assert with `pytest.raises(SystemExit)` + `capsys`.

6	the normative startup sequence (reconfigure stdout **and** stderr to UTF-8/`\n` before any output),
7	exactly-one-file reading via `utf-8-sig` + `newline=""` (D1), the exit-code matrix with
8	single-line `wordstat: error: ` messages and empty stdout on errors, the reserved exit-1 path (D3),

12	
13	In scope:
14	---
15	- `wordstat/cli.py`: add `fail(msg: str, code: int) -> int` (prints
16	  `wordstat: error: {msg}` to stderr, returns code) and
17	  `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` implementing the startup sequence from
18	  `feature-specification.md` §4:
19	  1. `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` and the same for `sys.stderr`
20	     — first thing, before argparse can emit anything.

22	  3. `try:` `open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="")` + `.read()` with
23	     `except OSError` → `return fail(f"{path}: cannot read file", 3)` and
24	     `except UnicodeDecodeError` → `return fail(f"{path}: not valid UTF-8", 3)`
25	     (`UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError`, not an `OSError` — separate clause, ordered first;
26	     `path` is the argument exactly as given).
27	  4. `result = count(text, args.top)`; `output = format_json(result) if args.json else format_text(result)`.
28	  5. Single `sys.stdout.write(output)` + `sys.stdout.flush()`.
29	  6. `except Exception` catch-all around steps 4–5 → `return fail(f"internal error: {e!r}", 1)` (D3);
30	     stdout must still be empty on that path (write happens only after formatting succeeds).

38	  `--json --top 2`; missing file; directory as FILE; invalid UTF-8 bytes; `--top 0`; unknown flag;

43	  and stderr contains no `Traceback`. (Valid file required so execution reaches `count()` —
